cultural.vision_reason: This is a machete with an English factory-made blade fitted with a locally made handle and elaborately decorated leather sheath in a geometric style typical of Hausa leatherwork; the blade being an imported trade good and locally re-mounted/sheathed is a common and accepted Hausa arms practice.

physical.title: machete; machete-sheath
physical.summary: Machete (a) with iron blade and riveted black plastic handle secured by nails and brass washers. Blade has straight top edge, lower edge has been reworked to form double-sided cutting blade which is curved at end. Three parallel grooves run 2/3 way along top half of blade. Inscribed with 'MARTINGDALE, BIRMINGHAM, MADE IN ENGLAND' on one side of blade. Sheath (b) made of thick cardboard covered with red-dyed leather. Painted linear decoration in black ink on one side of sheath. Two carrying-straps at side have undyed leather loops for suspension sewn onto leather flaps with red-dyed leather thong.
